gText_Answer.provenance: The Japanese corpus row is empty; こたえ is the Emerald cart's own word (gText_TheAnswer, "こたえは").

gText_BattleMenu.text: たたかう[CLEAR_TO 56]バッグ\nポケモン[CLEAR_TO 56]にげる
gText_BattleMenu.provenance: The Japanese cart's own words; only the alignment changes. The cart lines the two columns up with ideographic spaces ("たたかう　　バッグ / ポケモン　　にげる"), where every other cart uses the CLEAR_TO layout code ("FIGHT[CLEAR_TO 56]BAG / POKéMON[CLEAR_TO 56]RUN"). gen1recomp draws the four options in its own grid and splits the row into them at each line break and CLEAR_TO (src/core/game3/battle/ui.lua:2097, menu_labels), so the Japanese row gave it two options holding two words each and left the other two slots empty. The override keeps the words and puts CLEAR_TO 56 where the spaces were, as the US row does.

gText_CommaSpace.provenance: The Japanese corpus row is empty. The joiner the Battle Frontier puts between a list's species names (pokeemerald/src/frontier_util.c:1951); the cart's Japanese font has no comma, so items are separated with ・ as the cart's own rows separate words (サン・トウカ); requires in-game visual validation.

gText_ContinueMenuBadges.provenance: The label part of the cart's row ("もっているバッジ　[STR_VAR_1]こ"), which prints the value itself; gen1recomp's continue window draws the value in its own column (src/ui/game3/rse/main_menu_rse.lua:509-517).

gText_SpaceAndSpace.provenance: The Japanese corpus row is empty. The joiner the Battle Frontier puts before the last of a list of species names (pokeemerald/src/frontier_util.c:1949); と is the Japanese particle for "and"; requires in-game visual validation.

gText_Var1CertainlyHowMany2.text: [STR_VAR_1]　「[STR_VAR_2]」　を\nいくつ　おかいあげに　なりますか？
gText_Var1CertainlyHowMany2.provenance: The cart's own row, verbatim. It names the TM's move with STR_VAR_2, which the English line does not print but gen1recomp buffers for this key (src/ui/game3/rse/shop_menu.lua:240, say(shop, "gText_Var1CertainlyHowMany2", { name, moveName }), as pokeemerald/src/shop.c:1004 does).

gText_WhatWillPkmnDo.provenance: The Japanese cart's own words, broken after は like every other cart's two-line row ("What will / [B_ACTIVE_NAME_WITH_PREFIX] do?"). The Japanese cart prints "[B_ACTIVE_NAME_WITH_PREFIX]は　どうする？" on one line in its own, wider prompt window; gen1recomp draws the US window, whose right part the action menu covers (src/core/game3/battle/ui.lua:2123, action_prompt), so the line lost its ending.

gText_YesNo.provenance: The Japanese row of gText_YesNo is empty; the cart's other YES/NO menu row, e.common.berry_blender.sUnusedText_YesNo (same English), says it.

sText_AttackerUsedX.provenance: The cart's row is "[B_ATK_NAME_WITH_PREFIX][B_BUFF1]\n[B_BUFF2]": the particle and the ending appended to the move's name depend on the move (ChooseMoveUsedParticle and ChooseTypeOfMoveUsedString, pokeemerald/src/battle_message.c:2882, :2922). gen1recomp fills no particle and always appends sText_ExclamationMark (src/core/game3/battle/battle_text.lua:249), so the Japanese overrides give both the values of the moves outside sGrammarMoveUsedTable, most of them: the particle sText_ApostropheS ("の") here, and the ending sText_ExclamationMark5 ("！") under sText_ExclamationMark. The line reads "ポチエナの\nたいあたり！", as the cart prints it for those moves.

sText_ExclamationMark.provenance: The cart's sText_ExclamationMark5 row ("！"), the ending of the moves outside sGrammarMoveUsedTable (pokeemerald/src/battle_message.c:2922, case 4). gen1recomp appends sText_ExclamationMark to every move's name (src/core/game3/battle/battle_text.lua:249), whose Japanese row is the ending of a small group of moves ("を　つかった！"); see sText_AttackerUsedX.
